McLaren: McLaren’s latest tweaks sharpen the car’s rear‑end flow and add extra downforce with a high‑drag rear wing and beam wing, giving the car more bite in the corners and better stability on the straights. A modest front‑suspension update also improves reliability, so the team can push harder without worrying about mechanical gremlins. Together these changes should translate into more consistent lap times and a stronger attack on the podium this weekend.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has reshaped the airflow at the rear corner with a new scoop and winglet layout, giving the car more bite into the corners. At the same time, both the rear wing and the beam wing have been retuned for this circuit, delivering extra downforce when it counts and a cleaner, lower‑drag profile for the straights. The result should be a car that sticks to the tarmac tighter in the bends while still hitting strong top‑end speeds—exactly what they need to be competitive this weekend.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has tweaked the front of the car by reshaping the radiator opening and sidepods, giving the car a cleaner airflow that should boost straight‑line speed and cooling. At the rear, a new fairing around a suspension piece and re‑shaped wheel‑wake ducts tighten the aerodynamics, helping the car stay glued to the track in fast corners. Together, these changes aim to sharpen acceleration out of the DRS zone and improve rear‑end stability for the upcoming weekend’s high‑speed layout.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has tweaked the front of the car – the suspension fairings and front‑wing pieces have been reshaped to smooth the airflow, giving the car a little extra grip and stability into corners. They’ve also made a modest tweak to the engine‑cover shape to improve cooling for the specific demands of this circuit, helping the power unit stay in its optimal temperature window throughout the race. In short, the changes should make the car feel more planted and keep the engine humming, both key for a stronger performance this weekend.
Aston Martin: Aston Martin has fine‑tuned the rear‑halo area, the floor and diffuser, and reshaped the engine‑cover “coke” to smooth out airflow under the car, while the new beam‑wing angle slices a little drag off the rear. Those subtle shape changes give the car a steadier rear end and a little more straight‑line speed – exactly the kind of edge the team needs to fight for position this weekend.
Alpine F1 Team: Alpine has reshaped the front wing and its flaps, giving the car a cleaner, more balanced front end that should improve grip and cornering stability. They’ve also tweaked the rear bodywork panel around the engine cover to smooth the airflow, helping the car keep better speed on the straights. Together, these tweaks aim to boost overall handling and give the team a bit more pace over the weekend’s circuit.
Haas F1 Team: Haas has reshaped the front floor and narrowed its edge to tighten the airflow under the car, while a tweaked diffuser opening pushes a bit more down‑force to the rear. They’ve also refined the rear‑corner parts and lowered the rear‑suspension fairing to smooth the wake and improve balance. Together these changes should give the car a little extra grip and stability, helping the drivers extract more speed over the weekend’s corners.
Racing Bulls / RB: Racing Bulls has tweaked the underside of the car – reshaping the floor channels and moving the tiny wing‑lets that sit on the edges – to clean up the airflow under the chassis and generate a little extra grip on the corners. They’ve also sharpened the side‑pod cut‑out and added a small wing on the engine cover, which helps pull more air over the top of the car for better balance and stability. Together, these changes should give the RB a boost in cornering confidence and a tighter, more predictable feel on this weekend’s track.
